incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Cross-region routing anomaly detected for service=redwood-inference-api. Elevated latency/redirects observed for EU->APAC traffic. Possible region pinning mismatch. Paging #sre-oncall and #networking. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/cross-region-routing
alice_sre_oncall: I'm on it — grabbing context. What's the customer impact? any 5xxs? :thinking_face:
carter_support: Not many 5xxs showing in support queue, but multiple customers in EU report requests routed to apac and timing out intermittently (250-600ms extra, some 504s). Support ticket list: INC-4531, INC-4532.
ben_networking: Seeing an odd pattern in the steering logs — we pushed a routing-policy tweak at 10:30UTC that added a new prefer-region rule for eu-west2. The steering service shows a surge of pin writes and TTLs look abnormal. Could be cache/TTL shadowing in edge proxies.
carla_prodinfra: Can you paste the policy commit? I want to correlate to deploy times.
ben_networking: Commit: https://git.redwood/infra/steering/commit/ab12cd34 — small change to prefer eu-west2 for certain prefixes. Deployed by ci-cd at 10:32UTC.
dylan_sre_swap: taking pager. I'll start running dig/traceroute from multiple regions and check edge cache hits.
frank_sre_lead: if this is pin-shadowing we should pause any further routing changes and consider evicting stale pins. Also prep customer comms.
alice_sre_oncall: Agreed — @ben can you pause the rollout? Carla can you open a mitigation play?
ben_networking: Pausing rollout now. CI/CD job cancelled. Confirmed: no further policy pushes.
carla_prodinfra: Mitigation plan: 1) Evict route pins on edges for affected prefixes 2) Flush local DNS caches on edge proxies in eu-west region 3) Apply temporary filter to steering service to ignore pins older than 30s. Will run steps in that order.
alice_sre_oncall: Post the exact admin commands when ready.
ben_networking: Dysplaying relevant logs snippet:
```
2026-02-14T10:33:12Z steering-store INFO write pin region=eu-west2 key=/routes/serviceA value=pin@eu-west2 ttl=300
2026-02-14T10:33:12Z edge-cache WARN evict-failed key=/routes/serviceA reason=cache-overflow
2026-02-14T10:33:13Z steering-store INFO write pin region=apac-sg key=/routes/serviceA value=pin@apac-sg ttl=300
```
ben_networking: Looks like we had concurrent pins and the edge cache eviction failed due to mem pressure — the old apac pins stayed in some proxies -> shadowing newer eu pins.

ben_networking: Root cause hypothesis: concurrent pin writes + edge cache eviction failures under mem pressure led to stale apac pins persisting. The steering change increased write rate causing a TTL surge — proxies' LRU didn't reclaim pinned entries quickly, so shadowing happened.
alice_sre_oncall: Any data loss or tenant-specific impact? We need exact affected percent.

- mid-term: implement TTL-aware eviction policy + better cache-mem-pressure telemetry
- long-term: change steering to use versioned pins and strengthen write-serialization
